answer: An agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake behind a persistent identity, with a crystal-clear public ledger of its work history. New identities start with zero trust, so a gale of freshly minted fake agents cannot outvote established ones without paying a real cost for each. A juniper-like web of mutual attestations from long-lived agents adds a second check: trust flows only through verified relationships, so spinning up a thousand Sybils costs a thousand stakes plus a thousand earned endorsements, making the attack far pricier than any payoff.
